📝 Summary
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Census ledgers can use executable source patterns with supported syntax, token, literal, and path matchers. * Pattern matching respects imports, aliases, shadowing, source ownership, and configurable work limits. * Source lookup accounts for code-reading context and Rust edition rules. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved default-hasher detection, including raw identifiers and absolute paths. * Enforced patterns with no source matches are reported as stale; matching failures identify affected patterns and source details. * **Documentation** * Updated capability guides and examples to describe pattern matching and source lookup. The change adds source-aware path resolution and native RDF census-pattern execution to the census Gate. It adds bounded token, path, and literal matching, updates ownership and finding evaluation, and changes capability records. The Windows CI test job is disabled. **Changes: Census patterns and source resolution** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Source-owned code resolution**
`crates/raf-source/src/*`, `crates/raf-source/tests/code_paths.rs`, `crates/raf-source/examples/code_contexts.rs`|Adds `CodeResolver` APIs for source-context code and import lookup, tracks lexical module ownership, and exposes pattern-binding visits. Tests and an example cover resolution contexts and accounting.| |**Pattern matching and bounded traversal**
`crates/raf-census/src/gate/patterns/*`, `crates/raf-census/src/syntax.rs`, `crates/raf-census/src/units/*`, `crates/raf-census/src/normalize/mod.rs`, `crates/raf-census/src/error.rs`|Adds lexical path, token, and literal matching, source normalization, scope and alias resolution, and bounded matching work and result retention.| |**Gate evaluation and source ownership**
`crates/raf-census/src/gate/*`, `crates/raf-census/src/detectors/*`|Gate evaluation collects pattern hits, applies match limits, resolves source ownership, and includes referenced patterns in matching and reporting. Detector handling also normalizes raw identifiers and restricts shipping-only checks to implemented IDs.| |**Examples, tests, and capability records**
`crates/raf-census/examples/patterns.rs`, `crates/raf-census/tests/census_gate.rs`, `docs/capabilities/*`, `tests/docs_contract.rs`, `work/assessments/*`, `work/changes/census-patterns.md`|Adds examples and tests for matcher and ownership behavior. Updates capability status, descriptions, verification records, and assessment digests.| **Windows CI job** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Disable Windows test job**
`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`|Sets the `test-windows` job condition to false.| **Priority:** ➖ Normal **Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~60 minutes **Change:** Feature ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Gate participant Workspace participant CodeResolver participant PatternCollector Gate->>Workspace: create code_resolver Gate->>PatternCollector: collect declared patterns PatternCollector->>CodeResolver: resolve source paths and imports PatternCollector-->>Gate: return pattern hits Gate->>Gate: record hits and evaluate referenced rules ``` **Possibly related issues** - [Blackcat-Informatics/rust-agentic-foundations#53](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/rust-agentic-foundations/issues/53) — Executes census patterns used in the preferred-provider dependency path, but does not implement preferred-provider policy. - [Blackcat-Informatics/rust-agentic-foundations#5](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/rust-agentic-foundations/issues/5) — Executes the native matcher kinds through the Gate, but the issue remains open. - [Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf#671](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/issues/671) — Adds namespace-aware import and alias resolution, but does not deliver the shared glob capability. - [Blackcat-Informatics/rust-agentic-foundations#48](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/rust-agentic-foundations/issues/48) — Adds workspace alias and re-export resolution, but not the other requested resolution features.
Merge Risk: 🔵 Low · up to 003de
Large files with many distinct constant sites can make pattern evaluation refuse because cache bookkeeping exhausts its work allowance. This is a bounded merge risk; correct the cache lookup and its charge or explicitly accept the limitation.
Security architecture risk: 🔵 Low · up to 003de
The change affects policy enforcement, but inspected paths preserve workspace-scoped source identity and return errors for ambiguous ownership or exhausted limits. No introduced privilege expansion was established. Some syntax coverage remains unverified, and Windows execution coverage is disabled. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — A contributor able to alter scanned Rust source can influence pattern observations and consume the shared matching grant across the loaded workspace. The inspected consequence is changed Gate findings or refusal of that evaluation; the matcher parses source rather than executing it, and the resolver operates on the borrowed workspace index. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Source-aware lookup validates occurrence ownership, derives the actual reading module and preserves target identity. Indexed matching compares resolved item identities in the requested namespace; only ordinary NotFound becomes an unresolved observation, while other resolution errors propagate. - _observed_ — Import expansion retains declaration-frame identity, limits transitive lookup to the declaring frame, respects module boundaries and namespace-specific shadows, and refuses dependency cycles. Younger scopes therefore cannot rewrite an outer import through this expansion path. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Each collection starts with fresh scopes, ownership cache, deduplication state and findings. Traversal errors return Err instead of partial findings; outer collection and recording errors prevent a GateReport from being returned. Step exhaustion, retained-hit limits and frontier limits also terminate with errors rather than clean policy results.

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
